Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 30th June 2026
 
 
A Chara,  
 
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 & 
138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report for 
June 2026, detailing activities, updates, and progress across various departments of Louth County Council.  
 
Here is a summary of some key achievements and actions from the Chief Executive Report by Directorate for 
June 2026: 
 
1. Finance and System Support Directorate 
o 
Expenditure to 30 June 2026 was €89.2m (44% of annual budget), 
Income to 30 June 2026 was €93.9m (46% of annual budget). 
o 
805 IT support calls logged in June; 87% resolved the new help Desk Portal launched. 
o 
15% of inbound emails flagged as potentially harmful. 
o 
Website engagement remains strong, with planning and housing among the most accessed sections. 
o 
Cybersecurity training focused on phishing awareness. 
 
2. Economic Delivery Directorate 
o 
Louth Economic Forum met to discuss county economic profile. 
o 
Shopfront Improvement Grant Scheme open until October 2026. 
o 
Louth Tourism Strategy 2026- 2031 launched, aiming to position Louth as a leading sustainable  
tourism destination. 
o 
Supported diverse evening events, Pride programmes, and late-night museum/gallery access. 
o 
Hosted international delegations, launched Digitise Drogheda workshops 
and supported female entrepreneurship. 
o 
105 planning applications received, 92 were valid; 73 determined, with 10.96% refusal rate. 
o 
Dangerous structures: 16 files opened April–June; 11 entered on register. 
o 
Proposed variation to County Development Plan to align with national Guidelines- Variation No. 4. 
 
3. Operations & Environment Delivery Directorate 
o 
Extensive road repairs, drainage, footpath upgrades, and maintenance across Louth. 
o 
Ongoing litter picking, bin emptying, and illegal dumping clean-ups. 
o 
160 litter investigations, 44 fines issued, 137 waste complaints YTD. 
o 
Anti-Dumping Initiative funded for mattress/sofa amnesties and alley clean-ups. 
o 
Water, air, and noise pollution complaints investigated; farm and  
discharge inspections ongoing. 
o 
€651k allocated to 17 community climate projects. 
o 
Meadow Magic biodiversity project recognized nationally. 
o 
Council animal compound now nearly zero energy; distributed solar  
farm rollout underway. 
o 
30 dogs through the pound in June; 505 dog licences sold to June. 
o 
652 incidents YTD; ongoing training and new equipment procurement. 
 
4. HR, Corporate & Community Delivery Directorate 
o 
16,331 customer queries in June; 68% resolved at first contact. 
o 
Age Friendly initiatives, drama classes, and garden care projects ongoing. 
o 
Comhairle na nÓg and youth cross-border events held. 
o 
LEADER project funding approved for community projects. 
o 
Blue Flag beach season launched; Louth in Bloom competition underway. 
o 
Contracts signed for restorative justice and community inclusion projects.

6. Major Capital Projects & Infrastructure Delivery Directorate 
o 
Awaiting funding decisions for Drogheda and Dundalk regeneration projects. 
o 
Progress on St. Nicholas Quarter, Longwalk Urban Framework, and property vacancy initiatives. 
o

ogressing. 
o

o 
Corporate projects: Dominican Church/Library and Dundalk Fire Station Training Centre in design/pla
nning. 
o

o

o

o

o

Again I would like to conclude by expressing my sincere appreciation for the exceptional commitment, resilience, 
and professionalism demonstrated by the entire Louth County Council team.  
 
I encourage all members to read the report in full, which reflects the breadth, depth and impact of the remarkable 
work carried out across the organisation.

 Budget 2027 - Local Property Tax (LPT) Public 
Consultation 
 
The budget process for 2027 will begin shortly with 
the advertising of the Local Property Tax Public 
Consultation in July. The deadline for submissions 
from the public is Friday 21st of August 2026. 
 
The report will go to you, the members, at the 
September meeting where you can decide to set a 
local adjustment factor within the range of +25% to 
– 15% of the basic rate or may decide not to adjust 
the basic rate. If the rate is varied upwards 100% of 
the additional income will be available for the 
authority’s own use. Similarly, if the rate is varied 
downwards the loss of income will be reflected in 
reduced LPT funding to the authority. 
 
 
Budget Workshop 
 
We are proposing to hold a budget workshop for the 
members in September. Confirmation of the dates 
will issue shortly.

Louth Tourism Strategy Launch 
Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment 
Peter Burke TD, unveiled an ambitious new 
roadmap for the future of tourism in County Louth at 
the official launch of the Louth Tourism Strategy & 
Action Plan 2026 - 2031 at the Ballymascanlon Hotel 
& Golf Resort on Monday, 8th June. 
 
 
Louth Tourism Strategy Launch Event 
 
The strategy sets out a clear vision for County Louth 
to become one of Ireland’s leading sustainable 
tourism destinations, celebrated for its exceptional 
food, 
warm 
hospitality 
and 
authentic 
visitor 
experiences.  It aims to attract and inspire domestic

The launch event brought together tourism and

to grow and strengthen the county’s tourism sector 
in the years ahead.

Ireland’s leading sustainable tourism development 
agency, which explored the opportunities and 
ambitions set out in the strategy.
